hints: Start by drawing out the carbon skeleton of 3-methylpentane-1,3,4-triol and label each $\text{-OH}$ as primary, secondary or tertiary.
Remember that heating under reflux with excess dichromate(VI) gives the strongest oxidation, so a primary alcohol goes all the way to a carboxylic acid and a secondary alcohol goes to a ketone.
Check what happens to the tertiary alcohol in the middle and then join the three oxidised fragments back together in order.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting triol**

Lovely, let us first see what we have. Number the pentane chain 1 to 5.

$$\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(OH)-CH(OH)-CH}_3$$
C1 is $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, C3 is tertiary $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(OH)-}$, C4 is secondary $\text{-CH(OH)CH}_3$.

**Recall the oxidation rules**

This is the key idea. Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ oxidises by type:
$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid (with reflux, excess)}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction (resists oxidation)}$$

**Apply to each -OH group**

Now oxidise one by one. C1 primary under reflux with excess goes fully to $\text{HO}_2\text{C-CH}_2\text{-}$.
C4 secondary goes to a ketone, $\text{-CO-CH}_3$. C3 tertiary stays unchanged as $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(OH)-}$.

**Join to give the product**

Put the pieces back in order and you get:
$$\text{HO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{C(CH}_3\text{)(OH)COCH}_3$$
That is a carboxylic acid at one end, an untouched tertiary alcohol in the middle, and a ketone at the other end.

options.A: Correct. C1 primary alcohol is fully oxidised to $\text{HO}_2\text{C-}$, C4 secondary alcohol is oxidised to $\text{-COCH}_3$, and C3 tertiary alcohol is unchanged as $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(OH)-}$. This gives $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{C(CH}_3\text{)(OH)COCH}_3$ exactly.
options.B: Incorrect. This scrambles the carbon skeleton to $\text{-CO-C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)}_2$. The methyl group stays on C3 and no C-C bond cleavage occurs here, so the order of groups cannot rearrange like this.
options.C: Incorrect. This shows $\text{OHC-CH}_2\text{-}$, an aldehyde from C1. Aldehyde is only the product with distillation and limited oxidant. Under reflux with excess dichromate(VI), the primary alcohol goes all the way to the carboxylic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows $\text{-CO(CH}_3\text{)-}$, meaning the tertiary alcohol at C3 has been oxidised to a ketone. Tertiary alcohols have no H on the C-OH carbon and resist oxidation, so C3 must keep its $\text{-OH}$ group.
